findings.detail: No recognized acceptance of the revised Charter/grant exists. Maintainer direction on 2026-10-05 reframed the Charter (empty canvas whose users set direction; YOLO Dev as method, not product; product non-goals deliberately left open) and aligned the grant to the methodology, including a watermark convention for agent-created content. Cause: init proposes, humans accept. Impact: activation blocked; adoption stays state=proposed, qualification=unverified. Remedy: maintainer accepts the identified revision in issue #6, then Apply runs.

Reserved label yolo:state:deferred is absent. Cause: never created. Impact: the Postponed state cannot be represented; the app's own status contract cannot be fully exercised. Remedy: AI-maintained label creation, proposed as part of Apply after acceptance.

DECIDED under the grant's judgement clause: closed fixtures #2 and #3 retain yolo:state:* labels. Their purpose is to exercise the 'Status needs reconciliation' display that docs/verification.md cites as evidence; relabelling would destroy that trail. Retained deliberately as a cited deviation from the reserved-state rule, visible rather than repaired. Re-verify if a future request changes the display contract.

The YOLO status summary on #2 cites PR #1, which does not exist; no pull request has ever been opened here. Cause: the comment was hand-written during live verification. Impact: the summary demonstrates the format but not a real PR link. Remedy: treat as pre-adoption evidence with a known inaccuracy, not as delivery evidence.

DECIDED under the grant's judgement clause: add a real GitHub Actions workflow (npm test + npx tsc --noEmit on push and pull request) as ordinary work after activation. A placeholder job remains unacceptable. Until it exists, L1 evidence is harness-run and cited from docs/verification.md.

Harness version and fresh-session instruction loading are unverified; the adoption record leaves them explicitly open. Cause: this session is the installing session. Impact: Q1/Q5 cannot pass yet. Remedy: observe a fresh authorized session in this checkout and record the evidence.
Recognized maintainer evidence is direct: normzhou is the sole account with admin and push. No agent-supplied approver, and no grant has been self-certified.

.yolo/ contains only protocol.md, adoption.json, governance/ and reports/; governing roles use canonical slots; the shared bundle and bindings stay outside .yolo/; README links the governing documents.
Deterministic checks were re-run on the proposal subject and passed: 7 files / 64 tests, tsc clean, Node v24.21.0.
Architecture describes the smallest intended design and names the discrepancies (no CI, unexercised live paths) rather than ratifying them.

Agent-authored commits, PRs and issues post under the maintainer's account because the method and app reuse one authenticated gh session. DECIDED: agent-created content carries a 'yolo' watermark (PR title prefix plus visible footer and HTML marker naming the outcome issue), recorded in the authority document and AGENTS.md. Cause: no separate agent identity exists in the adopted methodology. Impact: without the watermark, human and agent action are indistinguishable in the record. Limit: the watermark is a recognition aid only; it neither authenticates the maintainer nor proves authority, and it may change with later YOLO Dev revisions.
